Looking at this problem, we need to find the last remaining number when we repeatedly remove elements at positions $1, 4, 7, \ldots$ (positions $\equiv 1 \pmod 3$).

## Key Recurrence

Let $S(n)$ be the survivor starting from list $1, 2, \ldots, n$. After one round:
- The list size reduces from $n$ to $m = \lfloor 2n/3 \rfloor$
- If the survivor of the reduced list is at position $j = S(m)$, its original position was:
  - $x = \frac{3j+1}{2}$ if $j$ is odd
  - $x = \frac{3j}{2}$ if $j$ is even

Both cases combine to:
$$S(n) = \left\lceil \frac{3 \cdot S(\lfloor 2n/3 \rfloor)}{2} \right\rceil, \quad S(1) = 1$$

## Depth Structure

Define the **depth** of $n$ as the number of iterations of $n \mapsto \lfloor 2n/3 \rfloor$ needed to reach 1. 

By induction, all numbers of the same depth have the same survivor. If $a_k$ is the survivor for any number of depth $k$, then:
$$a_0 = 1, \qquad a_k = \left\lceil \frac{3a_{k-1}}{2} \right\rceil$$

Computing this sequence:
$$\begin{align*}
a_0 &= 1 & a_1 &= 2 & a_2 &= 3 & a_3 &= 5 \\
a_4 &= 8 & a_5 &= 12 & a_6 &= 18 & a_7 &= 27 \\
a_8 &= 41 & a_9 &= 62 & a_{10} &= 93 & a_{11} &= 140 \\
a_{12} &= 210 & a_{13} &= 315 & a_{14} &= 473 & a_{15} &= 710 \\
a_{16} &= 1065 & a_{17} &= 1598
\end{align*}$$

## Depth of 2002

Tracing the reduction:
$$2002 \to 1334 \to 889 \to 592 \to 394 \to 262 \to 174 \to 116 \to 77 \to 51 \to 34 \to 22 \to 14 \to 9 \to 6 \to 4 \to 2 \to 1$$

This takes **17 steps**, so 2002 has depth 17. (Indeed, all integers from 1598 to 2396 have depth 17.)

Therefore, $S(2002) = a_{17} = \boxed{1598}$.
